findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap() on I/O Result panics on missing/unreadable file
findings.failure_mode: Any filesystem error (missing file, permission denied, empty path) causes a panic instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, _> and propagate with ? or map_err to a typed I/O error enum

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap() on ParseResult panics on non-numeric input
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV data with non-numeric second field causes a panic instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ...) and propagate through a Result return type

findings.problem: as u16 — lossy cast from u32 to u16 silently truncates values >= 65536
findings.failure_mode: A value like 70000 parses successfully into u32, then truncates to 4464 with no error, producing a silently incorrect Record
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(...) to produce a typed overflow error, or parse directly as u16 if the field is guaranteed to fit

findings.problem: .split(',').map(...).collect() — allocates a full Vec for every line when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per line; if a line has more commas than expected, the Vec grows unbounded instead of rejecting excess fields
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to extract name and value fields without collecting into a Vec, then trim each field independently

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into Vec with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: An empty line produces an empty Vec; indexing parts[0] panics with index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use parts.get(0).ok_or(...) or pattern-match on split_once result instead

findings.problem: parts[1] — unchecked indexing into Vec with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: A line with only one comma-separated field (no second field) produces a Vec of length 1; indexing parts[1] panics with index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use parts.get(1).ok_or(...) or pattern-match on split_once result instead

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — I/O side effect inside data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: Logging is mixed into the data-parsing pipeline, making the function impure, untestable, and producing hidden side effects in its core logic
findings.fix: Move println! to the imperative shell caller; the core parsing function should be pure and return data only

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes filesystem I/O (fs::read_to_string) with data parsing in a single function
findings.failure_mode: Cannot unit-test the parsing logic in isolation; every test requires filesystem fixtures; pure and imperative concerns are entangled
findings.fix: Split into parse_session_line(&str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> (pure core) and load_sessions(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> (imperative shell that reads, then delegates to core)

findings.problem: Returns Vec<Record> with no pre-allocation strategy; lines().map().collect() grows Vec with unbounded reallocations
findings.failure_mode: No attempt to handle Allocation errors; if the file is extremely large, repeated reallocations may exhaust memory before allocation failure is caught
findings.fix: Accept a pre-reserved Vec capacity (e.g., via metadata or try_reserve on a known line count) and handle Allocation errors explicitly

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 fields — no domain invariants enforced at the type level
findings.failure_mode: Any code can construct Record with empty name, invalid value, or inconsistent state without validation
findings.fix: Introduce a SessionName newtype with a fallible constructor that rejects empty names, and make Record a struct with private fields and a constructor that validates invariants

findings.problem: Record fields are pub — violates encapsulation; callers can construct invalid Records directly
findings.failure_mode: External crates can bypass validation by creating Record { name, value } without going through a constructor
findings.fix: Make fields private and provide a constructor or associated function that validates invariants

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data exists to show where time is spent in I/O vs parsing
no allocation tracing evidence (e.g., alloc counter or jemalloc stats) for Vec growth in load_sessions
no command-line interface or second-ring evidence for how load_sessions is invoked at runtime
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. All 10 findings are BLOCKER-level violations of Holzman Rust rules (unwrap, lossy as, unchecked indexing, no split_once, no try_reserve, functional core/shell violation, no domain types). The code would panic on any malformed input, silently truncate values, and cannot be unit-tested without filesystem setup. Fixing the 10 findings and establishing I/O boundary separation would be required before this crate could pass Holzman gates.
